whatItFakes: The laws listed in outcome-research-gaps.json (each with the outcome its research would measure) move no outcome-web measure: no researched link starts from the law or from a measure an engine sets from it, so the web holds those outcomes at their base whatever the law does.
why: data/research/outcome-web/links.json has no link from these laws or their measures; the laws' reach, engine reads and money are wired, but an outcome link needs a researched strength, shape and lag before the web can move anything.
replacement: A researched link per law in links.json (strength, shape, lag, source), built by the outcome-web line, after which each row leaves outcome-research-gaps.json.

whatItFakes: The web's youth firearm death and suicide rates become an expected count of young people lost in the town each month, but no named child dies of it.
why: Counted people die only through the illness-course engine (births-counted.ts); there is no injury death for a child.
replacement: PEOPLE: an injury death for full and counted young people, booked from this expected count.

whatItFakes: The immigration partnership moves the web's Hispanic school enrollment, undocumented employment and U.S.-born employment, but no school or jobs engine reads those measures.
why: The detainer holds are built; the three outcomes are kept place measures that no engine consumes.
replacement: WORLD and PEOPLE: school enrollment and jobs engines read the kept measures when they enroll and hire.

whatItFakes: The named residents' share of ordinary-crime arrests is carried in an unnamed batch of cases; no named person is arrested, held or sentenced by this engine.
why: A named person is charged only through an act the engines record (corruption cases today); there is no engine that records an ordinary offense as a named person's own act.
replacement: PEOPLE and GOV: an act engine where a named person's drives, record and circumstances decide an offense, then the case flow charges them from that act.

whatItFakes: A counted heir's relation to the person who died is read from the years between them (a parent's age younger, a child; older, a parent; nearer, the partner), so a counted sibling is taxed as a partner; and the estate is the dead person's share of their household's cash (the counts pool it in the group's account), not their own assets. A counted estate no one inherits is assessed against the state as heir, but a tax on that heir (where a statute taxes a government; none of the starting law's five does) is recorded as assessed and not collected, because the retired household's cash has left the pool.
why: The counts keep family pairs without their kind, so an inheritance tax class cannot be read from a counted record, and keep money by group, not by member.
replacement: The counted store keeps each family pair's kind (partner, child, parent, sibling) and each member's own assets, read for the estate and the inheritance class.

whatItFakes: The state's grant of local income-tax authority is read and recorded when a local body drafts an income-tax bill, and a state law row can grant or withdraw it, but no body can propose, enact or repeal the grant by bill.
why: A series a body can draft needs its bill-section words, which belong to the Words line (words-bill-section-local-income-tax-authority); the laws branch's own words were returned by Merger 2 on Oct 26.
replacement: Resolved Oct 28: the bill catalog offers law:local-income-tax-authority to state chambers (scripts/research/build-bill-catalog.py), worded by the Words row from #6432, so a legislature grants or withdraws its towns' power to tax income by bill and a town's next income-tax bill reads the law in force.

whatItFakes: A state that adopts an estate or inheritance tax by a bill that sets only a rate (it had none, so the bill has no schedule to keep) taxes the whole estate or share at that rate, with no exemption and no classes of heirs.
why: The bill catalog lets a legislature set the estate and inheritance tax amounts in any state; shapedRate keeps an existing schedule but a state without the tax has none to scale.
replacement: An adopting bill carries a schedule (an exemption, and for an inheritance tax the classes of heirs), drafted from the states that levy the tax.

whatItFakes: A government that takes an estate no one else does is assumed exempt from the state's inheritance tax where the law row carries no researched statute term for it: a state that adopts an inheritance tax by a bill (the bill sets a rate, not the statute's exemptions), and Kentucky, whose statute exempts transfers to cities, towns and public institutions in the state for public purposes without naming the Commonwealth itself, so the Commonwealth taking an estate by escheat is our reading of it. Maryland, Nebraska, New Jersey and Pennsylvania name the state itself and are quoted in data.
why: Every state with an inheritance tax in the starting law was checked against its statute (data/research/money/death-taxes-2026.json, governmentHeir, with cite, url and quote). All five exempt a government; four name the state, and Kentucky does so only by reading public institutions to include it. A state that adopts the tax by a bill has no researched statute.
replacement: A statute-cited governmentHeir term on every inheritance-tax row: an adopting bill carries its state's term (the engine taxes the government at the state's rate for others when the term says exempt: false), and Kentucky's Department of Revenue or a court confirms the Commonwealth is exempt as an escheat taker.

whatItFakes: The class of minor offenses the case flow models (disorderly conduct, drunkenness, liquor law violations, loitering and vagrancy) leaves out drug possession, and its police-staffing link takes the elasticity Chalfin, Hansen, Weisburst and Williams measured for a quality-of-life group that includes drug possession.
why: The owner's Oct 24 ruling names disorderly conduct, loitering and public intoxication 'and the like'. Drug possession is the largest part of the research's quality-of-life arrests, but it is also what the drug and cannabis laws change, so counting it here would put one arrest in two classes. Whether drug possession belongs in the class, or in a drug-enforcement class of its own that the same link moves, is the owner's call.
replacement: The owner's ruling on where drug possession arrests sit (docs/coordination/OWNER-DECISIONS.md), built as a second stream in the case flow with its own FBI arrest rate by state and the same police link.
resolution: Resolved by the Oct. 25, 2026 ruling (docs/coordination/OWNER-DECISIONS.md, laws lead, "Drug possession counts as low-level where the research class the PR uses says so"): drug possession is the sixth category of the minor offenses, on the same police-staffing link, with its own FBI arrest rate for each place (the sum of the FBI's five drug possession series, data/research/justice/low-level-arrests-2024.json, recorded ESTIMATED with the source), read by lowLevelStreams in src/core2/public-safety.ts through src/core2/low-level-offenses.ts; proved by src/core2/justice-low-level.test.ts.

whatItFakes: A bill the committee chair holds without a hearing keeps the chair's reasons on the committee record (their position on the bill, part by part, and what their temperament adds toward a hearing), but no scene, story or later decision reads them yet.
why: The reasons are the why of a held bill for the sponsor and the player; the scene where the sponsor asks the chair, and a story that a bill died without a hearing, are not yet built to read the record.
replacement: The sponsor-asks-chair scene and the held-bill press line read the chair's reasons by the committee record's id (laws-hold-record-names-the-sponsor).

whatItFakes: The law matrix grades the consumer-loan cap's outcome-web link from a declaration, not from a checker run: no law-wiring checker run shows the small-dollar lender reading the cap links' factor, so the cell quotes the lenders test's played-world records (src/core2/law-wiring-small-dollar-lenders.test.ts) and is graded partial, and the law counts as partly wired.
why: The checker (scripts/law-wiring/check.ts) changes a law once and leaves it to the world's own bills. The cap links lag 12 months (data/research/outcome-web/links.json). In Prescott, Michigan, the one checker place with a lender, the state legislature put the cap back with HB 4010 on 2025-08-04, seven months into the lag, so no month past the lag moved there. The places whose web ledger rows did move began with the cap (Vermont and Nebraska answer yes), and no lender opens where a state begins with the cap (smallDollarTerms in src/core2/modules/credit.ts), so nobody read those rows. The lenders test holds the law against the world's bills each day past the lag, which the checker does not.
replacement: A law-wiring checker run, in a drawn place with a small-dollar lender, that holds the law it changed against the world's own bills for the link's lag (as the lenders test's hold does) and records a loan whose web factor is below one (loan.webFactor and loan.webRecordId beside the month's record id), so the matrix grades the web link wired from the run; then this declaration is deleted.

whatItFakes: The social media age check law reaches a teen's mood through the youth gap in their resting stress: for a person aged 13 to 17 (socialMediaAgeFrom up to the voting age, the law's reach row), the age-gap term of restingStress (restingStressYouthWeight, the PSS-10 gap between ages 14 to 19 and adults) is multiplied by the outcome web's factor on health.youth-major-depressive-episode (age-verification-to-youth-depressive-episode), one for one with the share of teens in a major depressive episode. The whole youth gap is treated as the part of a teen's stress that tracks that share. No teen has a mood, depression or social media use record: the person's stress baseline moves for every teen in a place alike (the factor is the place's, not the person's own use), and the measure is the survey's 12 to 17 band applied to the law's 13 to 17. The link's size is an estimate from Australia's under-16 account drop, college-age studies of Facebook and of cutting social media, and a normal-threshold conversion to the share in an episode (data/research/outcome-web/links.json).
why: No engine keeps a teen's social media use or a depression condition, and no study sizes the law's effect on either. The one record that holds a teen's mood is the resting stress the person's affect returns to, which the full person (monthly) and the counted person (when a group decides) both read through restingStress, so reading the web there reaches both tiers by one rule.
replacement: The health engine keeps an adolescent depression condition per full teen (and a count for counted teens) decided from the teen's own traits, home and use, calibrated to the NSDUH share in an episode (health.youth-major-depressive-episode), with the web's factor multiplying that rate where the health engine decides it; a teen's social media use becomes a free-time act the age check removes for the teens it reaches; resting stress then reads the condition instead of scaling the age gap.
